edges.rationale: at r = 0, f̄(0) = f(0), so the inequality holds with equality

nodes.title: For r > 0, ∂²ḡ/∂r² = −(2/r²)(g − ḡ) + (4π/r²)(h − h̄)² g (p. 356)

edges.rationale: on the neighbourhood (0,∞) of r, deriv of the lift of ḡ is s ↦ (g(s⁺) − ḡ(s⁺))/s, so the second derivative is the derivative of this quotient
the numerator term g has derivative 4π g(r)(h(r) − h̄(r))²/r at r
the numerator term ḡ has derivative (g(r) − ḡ(r))/r at r
the quotient by s ≠ 0 has derivative ((g′ − ḡ′)r − (g − ḡ))/r², which simplifies to −2(g − ḡ)/r² + 4π g (h − h̄)²/r²
deriv of the lift of ḡ agrees with the quotient near r, so it has the same derivative at r
the numerator g − ḡ has derivative g′(r) − ḡ′(r) by the difference rule, and the denominator s ↦ s has derivative 1
